transcript: Birdie
Hi! I help businesses figure out exactly what they need from a chatbot. Before we start — what's your name?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh hi there! I'm Sandy, I own Furball Farmhouse Grooming and Daycare, it's out behind my house in the barn, well it used to be a garage but my husband Gary converted it, oh gosh that was years ago now, before Biscuit even had his hip troubles. Anyway sorry, yes, Sandy! Sandy Kowalczyk. Two Z's, everybody spells it wrong, even the vet gets it wrong and she's known me for years. What was it you needed again, hon?
Birdie

Hi Sandy! Great to meet you — Furball Farmhouse sounds like such a sweet setup. I'm here to get a clear picture of your business so we can build you a chatbot that actually helps. Let's start simple: what all do you offer at Furball Farmhouse — grooming, daycare, anything else?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh sure, sure. Well the big two things are grooming and the daycare, that's really our bread and butter. So grooming, we do the full works, bath, haircut, nails, clean the ears, the whole shebang, and then we also just do a quick bath and nail trim for folks who don't want the full cut, that's cheaper obviously. And then daycare, that's drop-in, people bring their dogs for the day while they're at work or whatever, Josh runs the play area on weekends, he's my neighbor's boy, still in high school, good with the dogs even though he's glued to his phone half the time, but aren't they all.

Oh and we do boarding too, overnight, I keep forgetting that one, isn't that funny, forgetting my own services. That includes a walk. And then we got the add-ons, flea and tick treatment, de-shedding, that kind of thing, for the dogs that really need it, some of these double-coated dogs, oh my word, the fur just does not stop.

Cats — no, we don't do cats, I keep saying I'm gonna start but I just... haven't. Been saying that for over a year now if I'm honest with you. Anyway! That's us in a nutshell I think. Did I miss anything, hon?
Birdie

That's a good rundown, Sandy! Let's put some numbers on these. Starting with the big one — the full grooming package (bath, haircut, nails, ears) — what do you typically charge for that, and how long does it usually take?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh boy, timing, hon, that's a good question, depends who you ask, Theresa's faster than me for sure, she just zips through, I always say she must've been a hairdresser in another life. Me, I take my time, especially if the dog's wiggly, we had a golden doodle last week just would not sit still, bless him.

But pricing, okay, focus Sandy — under 20 kilos it's $65, then 20 to 40 kilos it's $85, and then over 40, like your big fellas, Labs and Shepherds and that, it's around $110. Now giant breeds, like a Great Dane or a Mastiff, oh gosh, I honestly haven't nailed that one down, I've quoted anywhere from $100 to $130 depending on the dog and the coat and honestly my mood some days, don't tell Theresa I said that. We kinda just figure it out when they're standing in front of us.

Time-wise... honestly could be an hour, could be two, depends on the coat and if they're a good sport about the bath. Sorry, that's not a very exact answer is it.
Birdie

Got it, that's plenty exact for now, Sandy! For the giant breeds where it's a $100-$130 range decided on the spot — should the bot just quote that range and tell folks the exact price gets confirmed when they arrive? Or handle it some other way?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh yeah, that'd work perfect, just tell 'em "somewhere between $100 and $130, we'll nail it down when we see the pup" or something like that, don't wanna promise a number and then Theresa or me ends up eating the cost, ha. Oh that reminds me, we had a Great Dane in here, sweetest thing, drooled all over Theresa's apron, she was not thrilled, but anyway — yeah, the range is fine, hon, folks don't seem to mind as long as we're upfront about it.
Birdie
Perfect, got that wording down. Now the quick bath and nail trim option — what's the price for that one, and does it vary by dog size too, or is it a flat rate?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh that one's easy, flat rate, $25 no matter the size, big dog small dog don't matter, it's just a bath and the nails, don't take near as long. Although — oh my gosh, I remember this one time we had a St. Bernard in for that and Theresa said "flat rate my foot" 'cause the water bill musta tripled, ha, but no, we don't charge extra, $25 is $25. Poor Theresa was soaked head to toe after that one. Anyway yeah — $25 flat, hon.
Birdie
Ha, poor Theresa! Okay — roughly how long does that quick bath and nail trim take?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh gosh, um, quick one usually, twenty minutes maybe, half hour if they're squirmy about the nails, some dogs just hate that clipper sound, I don't blame 'em honestly, my knee surgery last year they had this little buzzy tool for something and I about jumped outta the chair. But yeah, bath and nails, twenty-thirty minutes, nothing like the full groom. Unless it's a big fluffy one, then you're drying forever, oh my word, the blow dryer just goes and goes. But average? Call it half hour, hon.
Birdie
Good, that helps. Now onto daycare — what do you charge for a drop-in day, and are there different rates for different days or sizes, or is it one flat price?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh that one's simple, thank goodness — flat $30 a day, drop-in, don't matter the size or the day, Tuesday same as Saturday. Or if folks are gonna be regulars we got the punch card, ten visits for $270, saves 'em a little bit, a lot of my regulars do that, the fella with the two beagles, oh my word those two are a handful, they come like three times a week. But yeah — $30 flat, or the punch card, that's it, hon.
Birdie
Love that, nice and simple. Now boarding — the overnight stay with a walk included — what's the price per night for that?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh yeah, boarding's $45 a night, that includes one walk, we don't skimp on that, dogs gotta stretch their legs. Speaking of walks, that reminds me, I gotta duck out here around 2 for Biscuit, he's my old fella, hip troubles, needs his slow little walk around then or he gets awful stiff, poor guy. Anyway — $45 a night, and we like to get 48 hours notice if you can swing it, just so we can plan around the other dogs and make sure Josh or Theresa's around if I'm not. Sometimes people call last minute though and we make it work anyway, hon, we're not too strict about it.
Birdie

Got it, $45 a night with a walk included, noted the 48-hour notice preference too. Now the add-ons — flea/tick treatment and de-shedding — what do those run, and are they add-ons to a grooming visit or can folks get them on their own?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh those, yeah, flea and tick is $15, and de-shedding's $20, and they're add-ons, hon, so they go along with a grooming visit, folks don't usually just come in for only that, though I guess we could do it if someone really wanted, we're not gonna turn away money, ha. De-shedding's a popular one honestly, especially in spring, oh my word, you should see the fur flying outta some of these dogs, we had a husky in here shed enough to make a whole 'nother dog, Theresa was picking fur outta her hair for days. But yeah — $15 flea/tick, $20 de-shed, tacked onto the groom usually.
Birdie
Perfect, that covers the services nicely. Now let's talk hours — what days and times are you open for grooming, daycare, and boarding drop-off/pick-up?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh sure, so we're open Tuesday through Saturday, 8 to 5, same hours for grooming and daycare drop-off and pickup and all that. Closed Sundays and Mondays — Monday's my catch-up day, laundry and paperwork and whatnot, gotta refill the shampoo bottles, oh and usually that's when I take Biscuit to the vet if he needs it, his hips have been acting up more this winter, poor old guy.

We're closed most holidays too, but I'll be honest with you hon, the sign out front doesn't always get changed in time, so sometimes folks show up on like Thanksgiving Monday and I gotta shoo 'em away in my bathrobe, ha, happened more than once. Gary keeps saying he'll make me a proper sign with the little clock hands you can move but he hasn't got around to it.

So yeah — Tuesday to Saturday, 8 to 5, that's us. Boarding drop-off and pickup, same window really, 8 to 5, we don't love doing it outside those hours 'cause somebody's gotta be there, but if it's an emergency we'll figure something out, we're not gonna leave a dog stranded.
Birdie

Good to know, thanks Sandy. Now, who's on the team and what does each person handle — I know you groom, Theresa grooms too, and Josh runs weekend daycare play — is that the whole crew, or is there anyone else, like who handles bookings or any disputes if something goes wrong?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh that's the whole crew, hon, just the three of us, small operation, that's kinda the charm of it I think, folks like knowing it's not some big chain thing. So me, I do most of the grooming plus all the paperwork and the phone and all that, which — oh gosh, I'm not great at the paperwork part if I'm honest, I got this notebook by the phone, just a regular old spiral notebook, that's our whole "booking system," ha, and don't I lose the darn thing about twice a year, drives Gary nuts, he'll find it in the fridge or somewhere and just shake his head at me.

Theresa's only in Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, but if you need a straight answer outta somebody, hon, call when Theresa's there, I mean that, she keeps saying she's gonna set us up with one of them Google Calendar things so we stop losing appointments, I keep saying "sure, sure" and then... well, you can guess, haven't happened yet.

Josh is just weekends, high schooler, watches the daycare pups play, sweet kid, little glued to his phone but good with the dogs.

And disputes or if something goes sideways — that's me, hon, that's all me, I handle that, though honestly it's usually just somebody forgot to tell us their dog's got allergies or something, nothing too dramatic, knock wood.
Birdie

That notebook system sounds like a real character, ha! Okay — when someone wants to actually book an appointment, how do they usually reach you: phone call, text, walk-in, anything like Facebook or Instagram messages?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh yeah, mostly folks just call, that's the old-fashioned way and most of my regulars know the number by heart practically. Some of 'em text now too, which, bless 'em, 'cause I don't always hear the phone ring out in the barn, the reception's just garbage back there, I don't know if it's the barn walls or what, Gary thinks it's the metal roof messing with the signal. So texts sometimes sit there for hours and I don't see 'em till I come up to the house for lunch or whatever.

Walk-ins happen too, especially in summer, folks just wander over from the road if they see the sign, well, if the sign's actually right that day, ha.

Oh and we got a Facebook page, my niece set it up for me years back, people message us on there sometimes, I forget to check it half the time if I'm honest, it's not really my thing, Theresa checks it more than me when she's in.

So — phone call's really the main one, hon, that's your best bet.
Birdie

That makes sense — phone reception in the barn sounds like a real headache! So what's the main thing you're hoping this chatbot helps with — is it mostly about catching those missed calls and texts, or something else on your mind?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh gosh, yeah, that's exactly it, hon, the missed calls and texts, that's the big one. I feel just awful when somebody's texted me at like ten in the morning asking about a groom and I don't see it till 3 'cause I been out in the barn or duckin' out for Biscuit's walk, and by then they've probably called somebody else, can't blame 'em. So if this little bot thing could just answer the easy stuff — you know, hours, prices, "yes we're open Tuesday," that sorta thing — while I'm elbow deep in soapy dog water, that'd be a load off.

And honestly, hon, if it could help me not lose track of bookings that'd be a miracle, that notebook, oh my word, Gary found it in the freezer once, don't ask me how it got there. Theresa keeps saying we need something better than my chicken scratch. So yeah — catching the messages I miss, and maybe helping with keeping appointments straight, those'd be my two big wishes. Did that answer what you were asking, or am I ramblin' again?
Birdie

That's really helpful, Sandy, and no, not rambling at all — that's exactly the kind of thing I need to hear! Given the notebook troubles, my honest suggestion would be a simple bot that answers the common questions and takes down booking requests (name, dog, service, preferred day) to send straight to you or Theresa, rather than a full payment/booking app with its own calendar — it solves the missed-message problem without you having to learn a whole new system. Does that sound like the right level for you, or would you rather look at something with online payment built in too?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh, that sounds just about right, hon, honestly. I don't need the fancy bells and whistles, my card machine's been broke since March anyway and I keep sayin' I'll replace it, Gary keeps sayin' it too, and neither of us do, ha. So no, skip the payment stuff, we're mostly cash or e-transfer anyway, people don't mind.

But yeah, if it just took down the name, the dog, what they want done, and what day works for 'em, and sent that straight to me — or heck, straight to Theresa on her days, she's way better about checkin' her phone than me — that'd be perfect. Long as it don't need me to learn some whole computer system, 'cause I'm tellin' you, I can barely work the one on the counter, Josh has to help me half the time and he's sixteen.

That's exactly the kinda thing that'd save my bacon, hon. That and findin' the notebook, but I don't think even your bot can help me with that one!
Birdie

Perfect, that's settled then — simple bot, no payment processing. When the bot takes down a booking request, who should it send that to — should it always go to you, or to Theresa on the days she's in (Wed-Fri)? And what's the best number for that?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh good question, hon. I'd say just send it to both of us if you can swing that, or if not, send it to me but CC Theresa on her days, Wednesday Thursday Friday, 'cause honestly she'll see it before I do most days, I might be out with Biscuit or elbow deep in some dog's ear. My cell's the best bet, it's 705-555-0192 — oh wait, no, hang on, is that right, I always mix up the last two numbers, Gary's the one who remembers stuff like that. Yeah, 705-555-0192, that's me. Theresa's got her own cell too but I don't rightly know it off the top of my head, I'd have to look in the — well, the notebook, ha, wouldn't that be funny. But yeah, text is way better than calling, hon, like I said, reception in the barn's just garbage, calls just ring and ring and I never even hear it.
Birdie

Got it, 705-555-0192, text preferred — that's noted. If someone reaches out after hours or on a Sunday/Monday when you're closed, what should the bot say — just that you're closed and give the hours, or something else?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh yeah, just have it say somethin' like "hey, we're closed right now, we're open Tuesday to Saturday 8 to 5, we'll get back to ya when we're open" — that oughta do it. Maybe don't even need to mention Sundays and Mondays by name, just the hours is probably enough, hon.

Oh and — this just popped in my head — maybe it shouldn't say anything about holidays, 'cause lord knows I don't even know myself half the time if we're closed for a holiday till the sign's already three days late getting flipped, ha, don't want the bot more organized than me and then me contradicting it. Just the regular weekly hours is fine, keep it simple.

But yeah — closed message, regular hours, "we'll be in touch," somethin' like that. That'd cover it, hon.
Birdie
That's simple and clear, good call. Quick one — do you need the bot to handle any language besides English, or is English the only one your customers use?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh, just English, hon, honestly. We're pretty small town out here, everybody's English far as I know, well except old Mr. Petrov down the road but he's got his granddaughter call for him anyway, sweet man, brings us these pickled beets every fall, don't even ask me why, but they're good actually. But no, English is fine, hon, don't need anything fancy on that front.
Birdie
Got it, English only, easy. Now — what happens if someone books a grooming or boarding slot and then no-shows, or needs to cancel last minute? Do you charge anything for that, or just let it go?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh, ha, well technically we got this 24-hour thing, like you're supposed to give us a day's notice if you're gonna cancel, I think Theresa's the one who came up with that, but honestly, hon, I almost never actually do anything about it, I just don't have the heart, people got sick kids or their car broke down or whatever, life happens. So it's "on paper" I guess but really I just let it go most times.

Now if somebody's a repeat no-show, like that one fella, oh gosh, forget his name, he stood us up three times for the same golden retriever, Theresa finally just said to me "Sandy, next time he calls just say we're booked," ha, so I guess that's our real policy, three strikes and Theresa gets mad. But officially? Nah, no charge, we're pretty easy about it. Maybe the bot could just gently mention the 24-hour thing so people feel like there's a policy, even if I don't really enforce it, ha, that'd be funny actually, more organized than me again.
Birdie

Ha, that's a fair policy honestly. One more on the practical side — roughly how many grooming appointments, daycare drop-ins, and boarding nights would you say you handle in a typical week, even just a rough guess?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh gosh, put me on the spot, hon, ha. Um, let's see... grooming, I'd say maybe 15, 20 a week? Depends on the week honestly, spring and summer get busier, everybody wants their dog looking spiffy for the warm weather, and then winter kinda dies down some, folks don't care so much if Fido's shaggy when it's snowing.

Daycare, oh that one's steadier, we probably got 8 to 12 regulars comin' in through the week, plus whoever just drops in random, like I said the beagle fella comes like three times a week on his own. So daycare-wise, maybe 20-some visits a week if you add it all up? Josh'd probably know better than me honestly, he's there watchin' 'em every weekend.

Boarding's the smallest piece, honestly, maybe 3 or 4 dogs a week stayin' over, sometimes zero if it's a quiet week, sometimes it spikes up around long weekends or when folks go on vacation, we had like six dogs boarding at once over the summer, oh my word, that was a full house, Biscuit didn't know what to make of it, poor guy just wanted his quiet corner.

So — rough guess, hon — groomin's the biggest chunk, daycare's steady, boarding's more here-and-there. That help any?
Birdie

That's really helpful, thanks Sandy. During those busier stretches — like summer or long weekends when boarding fills up to six dogs — do you ever have to turn people away, or is there some cap on how many dogs you can take at once?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh yeah, we definitely hit a wall sometimes, hon. I'd say six, maybe seven dogs boarding overnight is really our max, 'cause it's just me or Theresa or Josh keepin' an eye, and Biscuit needs his quiet corner too, poor old guy gets grumpy if it's too chaotic. So if somebody calls up wanting a spot over like the August long weekend and we're already full up, yeah, I gotta tell 'em sorry, we're full, try back or try somebody else. Doesn't happen too often, but long weekends and around Christmas, oh boy, everybody wants their dog boarded at once, funny how that works.

Daycare's a little more flexible 'cause they're not stayin' the night, but even then if Josh's got like fifteen dogs runnin' around on a Saturday, that's plenty, we don't want it turnin' into a zoo, ha. So yeah, there's a cap, just kinda goes by feel more than an actual number written down anywhere, if that makes sense.
Birdie

That makes sense, thanks. One more thing before we wrap up the details — have you got any old texts, Facebook messages, or voicemails from customers you could share? Even a few screenshots would help me ask sharper questions. You'd just pop them in the 'uploads' folder next to this program and let me know when they're in — or if that's a hassle, you could paste a couple of example messages here instead.
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh gosh, uploads folder, ha, you're talkin' to the wrong gal for that kinda thing, hon, I can barely find my email half the time, Josh usually has to log me in. But — okay, lemme think — I did just get Josh to help me before you called, so, yeah, I think I got a couple screenshots poked in there, some old texts and one of them Facebook messages from a lady askin' about the Great Dane pricing, funny enough. So yeah, hon, they're in there, uploads folder, should be good to go!

Oh and — reminds me — I gotta duck out here in a few for Biscuit's walk, it's near 2, but keep goin' if you got more questions, hon, I can text back after.
Birdie
No rush at all, hon — go give Biscuit his walk! Give me just a moment to look over those screenshots you and Josh put in the uploads folder, and I'll pick this up with you after.
Birdie

Okay, hope Biscuit enjoyed his walk! I had a look through what you and Josh uploaded — good stuff, it showed real conversations like a golden retriever booking and a pricing question, which matches what you've told me. One thing that came up a couple times: a customer named Marco asked twice, a week or so apart, whether you do cat boarding, and it looks like you told him you were still on the fence about it ('leaning towards no, ask me again in a month'). Where do you land on that now — should the bot just say 'not currently, dogs only' for cat boarding and cat grooming, or is that still genuinely undecided for you?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh gosh, Marco, yeah, he's a sweetheart, he's got that tabby, Mr. Pickles I think? Or was it Mr. Peppers, oh I can never keep it straight. But yeah, cats, cats, cats — honestly hon, I've been "thinking about it" for over a year now, Gary teases me somethin' awful about it, he's like "Sandy either do it or don't," but I dunno, cats are a whole different ballgame, they scratch different, they yowl different, Biscuit about had a heart attack the one time somebody's cat got loose in the waiting area, poor old guy just froze up.

So I'd say, for now, just tell folks "not currently, we're a dogs-only operation," 'cause that's the honest truth of where we're at, even if in my heart I might still come around to it someday. Don't want the bot promisin' cats when I can't even commit to it myself, ha. So yeah — dogs only, both grooming and boarding, that's where we land for now, hon. Maybe next year, who knows!
Birdie

That's a clear, honest answer, and I think it's the right call for now, Sandy. Last couple of quick ones: do you have any particular tone or name you'd want for the bot's personality — friendly and casual like you, or something else — and is there a rough budget or timeframe you're working with for this project?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh, tone-wise, hon, definitely friendly, casual, like you're talkin' to a real person, not one of them stiff robot-soundin' things, "please advise" and all that nonsense, drives me nuts when I call somewhere and it sounds like a computer readin' me my rights. Maybe give it a little personality even, folks around here like that homey feel, that's kinda our whole brand, the farmhouse thing, y'know?

Name-wise, oh gosh, I dunno, somethin' cute, maybe like "Barkley" or — oh, Gary just hollered somethin' from the other room, hang on — he says "Furbot," ha, that's actually not bad for him, might be onto somethin' there for once.

Budget and time, oh boy, that's more Gary's department honestly, he does the big financial decisions, I just sign where he tells me, ha, but I'd say we're not lookin' to spend a fortune, we're a little operation, so nothin' too fancy, and timeframe — sooner's better I guess, before summer gets busy again, that's usually when I'm drownin' the most and losin' the notebook every other week. Does that help any, hon?
Birdie

Love the homey vibe, and 'Furbot' is pretty cute, ha — Gary's not wrong! Before I pull together everything for you to double check, is there anything else on your mind about pricing or the business that we haven't covered yet?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh gosh, lemme think... I think we covered the big stuff, hon, my brain's kinda fried now honestly, all this talkin' about numbers, I'm more of a "figure it out with a coffee in hand" type person, not a spreadsheet person, ha. 

Oh! One thing, I dunno if it matters — sometimes folks ask if we do like, medicated shampoo or somethin' special for the itchy dogs, and we just use whatever Theresa's got in stock that week, we don't really have like an "official" list of that stuff, so maybe the bot shouldn't get too specific on that, just say "ask when you book" or somethin'. Other than that, I think you got it all outta me, hon, you're better at organizin' this than I am, that's for sure. Biscuit's good by the way, he did his little walk, real proud of himself, tail waggin' the whole way, poor old guy.
Birdie

Glad Biscuit had a good walk! Okay Sandy, let me read back everything I've got so you can check it over:

**Business:** Furball Farmhouse Grooming and Daycare, run out of a converted barn behind your house. Team: you (grooming, phone, bookings), Theresa (grooming Wed-Fri, checks Facebook, tracks holiday info), Josh (weekend daycare supervision, helps with tech). Gary handles budget decisions.

**Services & pricing:**
- Full groom: under 20kg $65, 20-40kg $85, over 40kg ~$110, giant breeds $100-$130 (confirmed in person) — roughly 1-2 hrs
- Quick bath & nail trim: flat $25 — 20-30 min
- Daycare drop-in: flat $30/day, or punch card 10 visits/$270
- Boarding: $45/night incl. one walk, 48hr notice preferred but not enforced
- Add-ons: flea/tick $15, de-shedding $20 (usually with a groom, can be standalone)
- No cat services — dogs-only, firmly, for now
- Medicated shampoo: varies by stock, no fixed list — bot says 'ask when you book'

**Hours:** Tue-Sat 8-5, closed Sun/Mon and most holidays (dates not tracked reliably). Bot should just give the weekly hours, not mention specific closed days or holidays.

**Policies:** Cash or e-transfer only (card machine broken); 24-hr cancellation policy exists on paper but isn't enforced — bot can mention it anyway; repeat no-shows (3+) get turned away in the future; boarding caps around 6-7 dogs, daycare caps around 15 dogs, both by feel not fixed numbers.

**Channels:** phone, text, walk-ins, Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp. English only.

**Volume:** ~15-20 grooms/week, ~20+ daycare visits/week, ~3-4 boarding stays/week (spikes to 6 on busy weekends).

**Handoff:** booking requests texted to Sandy at 705-555-0192, CC'd to Theresa on her days if possible (her number still TBD). Disputes go to Sandy directly.

**Bot scope:** simple bot — answers FAQs, takes booking requests (name, dog, service, day) and forwards them — no payment processing, no full booking app.

**Tone:** friendly, casual, homey farmhouse feel. Name: leaning toward 'Barkley' or 'Furbot' (not fully decided).

**Budget/timeline:** no fixed budget (Gary's call, but modest), hoping to have this sorted before summer rush.

Does all that look right, or anything you want to change?
Sandy Kowalczyk

Oh that's a lot to take in, hon, good job keepin' it all straight! Let's see... yeah that's mostly spot on, real close.

Couple little things though — I don't think I ever said anything about WhatsApp, hon, we're not on that, just phone, text, walk-ins, and the Facebook Messenger thing, that's it, no WhatsApp over here, ha, wouldn't even know how to work that one.

And Theresa trackin' holiday info — no, hon, nobody tracks that, that's kinda the joke, the sign just don't get changed in time, nobody's in charge of holidays, it just... happens, or don't happen, ha.

Everything else though, yep, that's us to a T, you got it all outta me somehow! Real impressive, hon.
Birdie

Perfect, thank you Sandy — fixed both of those (no WhatsApp, and no one officially tracks the holiday hours, that's just how it goes!). That's everything I need for now. Thanks so much for all the great detail today — this'll go to the build team to put together, and someone will follow up with you on next steps. Enjoy the rest of your afternoon with Biscuit!

brief.business_description: Runs grooming and daycare business out of a converted barn/garage behind her house, converted by her husband Gary. Team of three: Sandy (does most grooming plus paperwork/phone/bookings), Theresa (grooms, works Wed-Thu-Fri, faster than Sandy, more reliable for a straight answer, also checks Facebook more often), Josh (neighbor's son, high schooler, watches daycare play area on weekends, also helps Sandy with computer/counter stuff). Sandy handles disputes/issues personally (usually just missed allergy info, nothing dramatic). Gary handles the big financial/budget decisions for the business. Nobody is officially in charge of tracking holiday hours - it's not written down anywhere, which is why the sign out front often doesn't get updated in time.
brief.problem_to_solve: Missed calls and texts (poor cell reception in the barn) cause lost business - wants the bot to answer easy questions (hours, prices, open days) while she's busy. Also hopes it can help keep track of bookings better, since current system is a spiral notebook that gets lost/misplaced (once found in the freezer).
channels: Phone calls (main way customers reach them)
Text messages (sometimes missed for hours due to poor cell reception in the barn)
Facebook Messenger (niece set up their page; Sandy rarely checks it, Theresa checks more often)
integrations: Current booking system: a spiral notebook by the phone (no digital system); Theresa has suggested moving to Google Calendar but it hasn't happened yet
brief.conversation_volume: Rough weekly volume: ~15-20 grooming appointments (busier spring/summer, slower winter), ~20+ daycare visits (8-12 regulars plus drop-ins), ~3-4 boarding stays typically (0 in quiet weeks, spikes to ~6 dogs at once over long weekends/summer vacations).
brief.budget: No specific figure given - Sandy says budget decisions are Gary's department, but 'nothing too fancy,' fitting a small operation.
brief.timeline: No firm date - Sandy would like it 'sooner' and ideally before summer, which is her busiest and most overwhelmed season.
services_and_pricing: Full grooming (bath, haircut, nails, ears): under 20kg $65; 20-40kg $85; over 40kg (Labs, Shepherds, etc.) ~$110; giant breeds (Great Dane, Mastiff) $100-$130, exact price confirmed in person - turnaround roughly 1-2 hours depending on coat and dog's temperament
Quick bath & nail trim: flat rate $25 regardless of size - turnaround about 20-30 minutes on average (longer for big fluffy dogs needing extra drying)
Daycare (drop-in, dogs only): flat $30/day regardless of size or day of week; punch card option - 10 visits for $270
Boarding (overnight, includes one walk): $45/night; 48hr notice preferred but not strictly enforced
Add-ons (usually tacked onto a grooming visit, but can be done standalone if requested): Flea/tick treatment $15; De-shedding $20 (popular in spring)
No cat services currently offered - dogs-only operation, both grooming and boarding
Medicated/specialty shampoo for itchy dogs: no set product or official list - varies week to week based on what Theresa has in stock; bot should say 'ask when you book' rather than naming specifics
faq_answers: Giant breed grooming price: bot should say 'somewhere between $100 and $130, we'll nail it down when we see the pup' rather than quoting an exact number upfront

Out-of-hours/closed message: bot should say something like 'we're closed right now, we're open Tuesday to Saturday 8 to 5, we'll get back to ya when we're open' - just regular weekly hours, no mention of specific closed days (Sun/Mon) by name, and no mention of holiday closures since even Sandy doesn't always know in advance.
Cat boarding/grooming: bot should say 'not currently, we're a dogs-only operation' - Sandy has been undecided for over a year but wants a clear, firm answer given to customers for now.
Medicated/specialty shampoo question: bot should say 'ask when you book' since there's no fixed product list, it varies by what's in stock.
business_policies: Boarding: prefer 48 hours notice so they can plan staffing (Josh/Theresa coverage), but not strictly enforced - last-minute bookings are often accommodated

Hours: Open Tuesday-Saturday 8am-5pm for grooming, daycare, and boarding drop-off/pickup. Closed Sundays and Mondays (Monday is catch-up/admin day). Closed most holidays, though nobody officially tracks holiday dates and the posted sign isn't always updated in time. Boarding drop-off/pickup normally same 8-5 window since staff need to be present, but emergency exceptions are made so a dog isn't left stranded.
Payment: mostly cash or e-transfer; card machine has been broken since March and not yet replaced, so no card payments currently accepted.

Cancellation policy: officially a 24-hour notice policy for cancellations (Theresa's idea), but Sandy rarely enforces it and doesn't charge for late cancellations or no-shows - she lets it go out of sympathy. Repeat no-shows (3+ times) result in Sandy declining to book that customer again in future. Sandy is fine with the bot mentioning the 24-hour notice policy even though it isn't strictly enforced in practice.

Capacity limits: boarding max is about 6-7 dogs overnight at once (limited by staff supervision - Sandy/Theresa/Josh - and Biscuit needing his quiet corner); daycare max is roughly 15 dogs on a busy Saturday under Josh's supervision. No hard written number - goes by feel. During long weekends/Christmas, boarding fills up and they turn people away.
escalation_rules: Booking requests should be sent to Sandy's cell, 705-555-0192 (text preferred over calling, since barn reception doesn't pick up calls well). If possible, also send/CC Theresa on her working days (Wed/Thu/Fri) since she checks her phone more reliably; Theresa's own cell number is not yet available - Sandy would need to look it up.
Disputes or anything going sideways (e.g. undisclosed allergies) are handled personally by Sandy.
open_items: Theresa's direct cell number not yet provided - Sandy needs to look it up.
Exact capacity limits for boarding (6-7) and daycare (~15) are approximate/by feel, not fixed numbers - bot should treat these as guidance, not hard rules, when taking booking requests near capacity.
Bot name/persona: Sandy is leaning toward something cute like 'Barkley' or Gary's suggestion 'Furbot' - not fully decided.
additional_notes: Scope decision: Sandy wants a simple bot (answers FAQs, takes booking requests with name/dog/service/preferred day and forwards them) rather than a full booking/payment app - confirmed, no card payment needed since card machine is broken and they use cash/e-transfer.
From uploaded chat samples: a customer named Marco P asked twice (weeks apart) whether they offer cat boarding - now resolved as 'dogs-only, not currently.'
Tone: friendly, casual, homey 'farmhouse' personality - not stiff or robotic.

inquiry_categories: Appointment booking/scheduling for grooming services (~30%) - customers requesting specific dates/times for dog grooming appointments
Pricing inquiries for specific breeds/services (~25%) - customers asking cost of full groom, add-ons like nails or deshedding based on dog size/breed
New service availability requests (~15%) - customers asking if business offers services not clearly established yet, e.g., cat boarding/grooming
Business hours inquiries (~10%) - questions about holiday or long-weekend operating hours
Drop-off/logistics coordination (~10%) - minor scheduling adjustments like early drop-off times
Post-service follow-up and rebooking (~10%) - customers confirming satisfaction and scheduling next appointment
resolved_patterns: Booking a grooming appointment: Customer asks for a date/time, staff (Sandy) confirms availability directly in chat and checks the paper appointment book to verify the correct date (e.g., Karen T's Thursday booking for golden retriever, confirmed as Thursday the 10th at 10am).
Pricing for standard breed groom: For a golden retriever full groom, staff quoted $85 base price, noting the 20-40lb size range applies, with an optional $20 deshedding add-on for heavy-coated dogs.
Drop-off time flexibility: When customer asked to drop off 15 minutes early, staff immediately approved without hesitation ('oh totally fine').

Rebooking cadence for goldens: After a completed groom, staff proactively suggested shortening the rebooking interval from 6 weeks to 5 weeks for golden retrievers due to fast undercoat growth, leaving final decision to customer.
knowledge_gaps: Cat boarding availability: Marco P asked twice (Apr 8 and Apr 16) if the business offers cat boarding. Staff repeatedly said she hadn't decided ('let me think on it', 'haven't fully decided, leaning towards no... ask me again in a month'). No firm policy exists - owner needs to clarify whether cat boarding/grooming will be offered and under what conditions.

Pricing for large/giant breeds (e.g., Great Dane): Deb R asked for full groom + nails pricing for a Great Dane. Staff was unsure of exact price ($100 vs $110, confused with a mastiff job) and said 'let me look and get back to you.' Customer followed up days later with no resolution shown in the materials - exact pricing rules for oversized breeds need to be defined.

Holiday/long-weekend hours: Priya S asked if the business is open on Easter Monday. Staff did not know and said she'd have to check with another staff member (Theresa) who 'keeps track of that stuff.' No resolution shown - official holiday hours policy needs to be documented.

Cat grooming as a general service line: Referenced in the boarding conversation ('I've been going back and forth on whether to even do cat grooming'). Not a firm inquiry but reveals an unresolved business decision that could generate customer questions the bot can't answer confidently.

Golden retriever full groom price: $85; deshedding add-on: $20 extra
Large breed (Great Dane) full groom + nails pricing is inconsistently recalled by staff (~$100-110), not standardized

Business uses a punch card loyalty program (physical cards, stock tracked manually)
Recommended re-groom interval for golden retrievers is approximately 5-6 weeks
Business is located in a region near Barrie, Ontario (referenced via staff's sister's wedding location), suggesting Canadian/Ontario operations
Business does not currently have a dedicated setup for cat boarding ('mostly a dog space')
